chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from al-Mu'afi ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

It is no objection if a man prays in the Masjid al-Shajara and says what he wishes to say, and does not say the Talbiyah, then he goes out and catches game or other things, there is no blame on him for that.

key_terms.الصَّيْدُ: Game (wild animals), the catching of which is prohibited for a Muhrim (one in Ihram).
key_terms.فِيهِ شَيْءٌ: Any blame or penalty (in this context, the fidyah for catching game).
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible.
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الشَّجَرَةِ: The Mosque of the Tree, a specific location near Mecca associated with the Prophet's journey.
key_terms.يُلَبِّي: He recites the Talbiyah, the specific declaration 'Labbayk Allahumma...' signifying the formal entry into the state of Ihram.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on catching game if one prays at Masjid al-Shajara without reciting the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the distinction between the physical state of Ihram and the ritual declaration (Talbiyah), establishing that praying in Masjid al-Shajara prior to the formal commitment allows one to avoid the penalty for hunting game. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition of hunting applies specifically after the pilgrim has verbally or mentally committed to the state of Ihram, offering practical flexibility for travelers in the Meccan vicinity. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and declaration in determining the applicability of Ihram restrictions.
